claims.quote: We collected structural brain MRI and cognitive-behavioral data from 40 pre-pubertal children with Noonan syndrome (NS), caused by PTPN11 (n = 30) or SOS1 (n = 10) variants (age 8.53 ± 2.15, 25 females), and compared them to 40 age- and sex-matched typically developing controls (9.24 ± 1.62, 27 females).

We collected structural brain MRI and cognitive-behavioral data from 40 pre-pubertal children with Noonan syndrome (NS), caused by PTPN11 (n = 30) or SOS1 (n = 10) variants (age 8.53 ± 2.15, 25 females), and compared them to 40 age- and sex-matched typically developing controls (9.24 ± 1.62, 27 females).
In NS, we observed smaller volumes of bilateral striatum, precentral gyri, and primary visual area (d's < -0.8), and extensive effects on SA (d's > |0.8|) and CT (d's > |0.5|) relative to controls.
